heading: Determinism & bit-identity
text:
### Determinism & bit-identity [IRET.28.10]

This section is normative. Iteration order is deterministic, as cross-platform
bit-identity requires (`[LDET.3.4]`), and it does not decide rule-firing
order: `[LDET.5.5]` orders a rule's activations by a key computed from the
match and working memory, so the engine **must not** derive a timetag from the
order in which it traverses these tables (`[LDET.5.9]`).

idris.name: ldet_5_9__dense_refuted
idris.note: Witnesses the prohibition: a timetag derived from the dense traversal order orders one rule's activations differently in a run and its replay by assertion, against [LDET.5.9]. Rule `A a, B b`; assert b1, b2, b3; retract b1; assert a1 -- the run's B memory is [b3, b2], the replay's [b2, b3]. Under the [LDET.5.5] key both give (a1, b2) then (a1, b3): `ldet_5_5__canonical_agrees`, `ldet_5_9__network_agrees`.
